description: Recommends new policy to incentivize affordable housing city-wide.
Expands market housing incentives to established neighborhoods.
Removes vacancy requirements for development incentives.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
4 for, 2 against
Patrick Wolfe stated infill is a "cash cow" for the city, suburban development a "money pit."
Developers face high costs for land assembly in established neighborhoods.
Committee expanded incentives beyond administration's recommendation for targeted growth areas.
No specific cost-benefit analysis for infill versus greenfield development was presented.
Development community advocated for broader incentives to overcome high infill costs.
Mayor Block was reluctant to expand incentives without further public and developer consultation.
Affordable housing incentives target low-income levels using provincial income maximums.
